newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle mission nears end.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle mission nears end.

text.p: Astronauts aboard the space shuttle Columbia said on Tuesday they looked forward to returning to earth after a trouble-free reflight of a science mission cut short in April because of a defective power generator.
"We'll certainly be glad to go home," shuttle commander Jim Halsell told a news conference. "We have completed our tasks just about."
Columbia is due to land at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Thursday at 6:47 a.m. EDT (1047 GMT).
The shuttle's first attempt at the 16-day mission was aborted in April after only four days aloft because of a troublesome electricity-generating fuel cell.
In an unprecedented move, NASA ordered Columbia and its crew back to space to finish work on the $86 million package of scientific experiments.
"As much as the other one was a bummer, this one is a real trip," guest scientist Roger Crouch said.
Halsell said Columbia, the oldest shuttle in NASA's fleet, "performed absolutely flawlessly" the second time around.

Since blasting off on July 1, Columbia's crew has ignited more than 200 fires for combustion research in the shuttle's bus-sized laboratory. The mission's 30 other experiments included studies on plant growth and the development of new alloys and semiconductors for the electronic industry.
Astronaut Janice Voss said NASA was thinking about adding more science missions to the shuttle's flight schedule.
